访谈笔记 — 傍晚通勤
1st November 2026 at 5:56pm
interviews
reading
synthesis
A route remembered through small anchors

This synthetic interview carefully combines several invented accounts into one reading sample. The speaker is a fictional participant, Lin, who walks from a bus stop to the waterfront workshop twice a week. None of the quoted material represents a real person.

“I know I am nearly there when I can see the narrow bakery window. I do not remember the street name. The map says the route is simple, but the map cannot tell me which crossing will feel busy.”

从描述到问题

林将路线分成三个片段：离开车站、经过商店、进入临水步道。她并没有把每个转角都当作同等重要的决策。车站附近的选择最多；中段主要依靠店面的顺序；接近目的地时，她开始留意灯光和人流。

这提示我们检查信息出现的时机。把所有路名放在同一块牌子上，也许能够提高地图的完整性，却不一定减少第一次经过时的判断负担。一个人可能先需要知道「沿着有店面的这一侧走」，然后才需要确认目的地的具体入口。

Detail worth keeping

The bakery window mattered because it remained visible when the bus shelter hid the next sign. A useful landmark was therefore not simply a memorable object. Its usefulness depended on the approach direction, other people in the street, and the distance from the decision point.

The participant described a change in confidence after passing the second crossing. That is an account of experience, not a timed behavioural measurement. We should not infer that a particular sign caused the change until the sequence is examined more carefully.

同一路线的不同体验

下雨时，林会选择多走一小段但有连续屋檐的路线。提着材料时，她愿意等一次较长的红灯，避免在狭窄的路段挤过行人。她认为两条路线都「不远」，但在不同的晚上会选择不同的一条。

我们需要保留这种条件差异。研究工作台不能只留下一个看似确定的结论，例如「参与者偏好最短路线」。若笔记中的约束、例外和反例被视觉层级压得太轻，团队很容易只记住标题。

Open interpretation

A tentative hypothesis is that route confidence grows when a person can predict the next visible anchor. A competing hypothesis is that familiarity with the neighbourhood matters much more than the signs. Both remain plausible within this invented material.

In a follow-up, ask the participant to narrate the journey before showing any alternative map. Invite them to identify the point where they would be comfortable putting the phone away. Then inspect what could be seen from that point and what could not.

Notes for editing
Preserve the distinction between the speaker's account and the researcher's hypothesis.
Keep long English passages readable beside Chinese paragraphs.
Retain meaningful headings when moving between reading and editing.
Return to the same note after checking Evidence ledger.
A final unresolved question

如果标志必须很少，我们应该优先标出第一次进入街区的方向，还是优先帮助已经走错的人找回路线？这两种目标可能需要不同的信息位置。下一轮访谈应当分别追问，而不是用一个笼统的「导航是否清楚」覆盖它们。
